# Lecture 1 — transcript

¶1 Auzubillah Minashaitan Nirajeem

¶2 Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim

¶3 We start our sessions on Irfan ie Islamic Mysticisim. Of course we are going to have a very short introduction about this topic and we will start the real lesson from next week. Islamic mysticism, mysticism is very mysterious. No one knows what mysticism is. Really even the mystics themselves are in doubt about what mysticism really is except the real mystics. Mysticism is not of course limited to Islam. Even non-religious people, some of them have some kind of inclination and that's why it makes the whole issue more difficult to actually distinguish between Islamic mysticism and other types of mysticism which is very important. Also mysticism is for many, many different reasons like if someone wants some extraordinary power or someone say for example wants to be in 2 places the same time, they seek mysticism and they want to explore the mysteries of the unknown world of human soul so that they have some power.

¶4 That is one kind of mysticism which we find in other religion. While we have to distinguish that one from real mystic therefore, the first thing is that what are we going to talk about and what do you want and who are mystics? What do they want when they said about on this very difficult course of their journey which is really exhausting, time consuming, life consuming and especially when we come to the saying of our immah and also some verses of the Quran, we find the type of mysticism that included in their supplication, their words which are somehow very different from other type of mysticism that we find in other religion. Therefore, we have to find what we after are and what we are going to talk about.

¶5 Now we want to know why mystics actually say about this mystical journey towards the lord. I mean, everyone can be honest and someone went to the prophet and said I don't have that eagerness and enthusiasm to perform salatul-layl and mustahab fasting and all these things. If I pray my 5 times duty prayer and I fast in Ramadhan and pay my zakat and once go to hajj, will I go to jannah? Prophet said, yes. If you do these things you go to jannah. So why should we work so much if it’s so easy to go to jannah just by performing our wajib duties? Why should we seek this type of hard endeavour which is mysticism? Why should we do?

¶6 Are we encouraged to do that? Because some people you know that some Muslims jurist and some Muslim activists, they are completely against mysticism because they say whatever the shariah has told you, you follow and you go to jannah and there is no other way. Mysticism is something silly to follow and it is made up by some mystics according to their vibes and wishes. So is that true? What the quran says about mysticism? Let’s see. I have chosen some part of verses from Surah Rum which you can find many other verses in the same line. Now it says “Wa min Aayaatiheee an khalaqa lakum min anfusikum azwaajal litaskunooo ilaihaa wa ja'ala bainakum mawad datanw wa rahmah; inna fee zaalika la Aayaatil liqawminy yatafakkaroon” 30:21and one of the signs is that he created mates for you from yourself that you may dwell in tranquillity with them and He has put love and mercy between your (hearts): verily in that are Signs for those who reflect.

¶7 What signs? Does everyone see signs of god in this and when you look into such a relationship between man and woman, do you see the sign of god in that? Do we see that? Usually will see the sign of shaitan, isn’t it? But there are signs for the people who reflect. So signs are there but not for everyone but for the people who reflect. The next verse, “Wa min Aayaatihee khalqus samaawaati wal aardi wakhtilaafu alsinatikum wa alwaanikum; inna fee zaalika la Aayaatil lil'aa”imeen" 30:22 and from the signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your tongue and colors, verily in that are Signs for those who know. There is an argument because if you have different, ethnicities racism this is what we see in this.

¶8 What sign of God we see in this? Of course there are signs in this for the knowledgeable. There are signs in this for the learned. Not for everyone. If you see signs in this you are learned but not most people, not even most pious people and not even most people who are very stipulant about shariah find signs in this. Now the verse continuous, “Wa min Aayaatihee manaamukum bil laili wannahaari wabtighaaa'ukum min fadlih; inna fee zaalika la Aayaatil liqawminy yasma'oon” 30:23 And among His Signs is the sleep that you take by night and by day, and the quest that you (make for livelihood) out of His Bounty: verily in that are signs for those who hear.

¶9 Aren’t we hearing? Do we hear? If we hear why when we see these signs we are not broken down as the prophets or the awliyaallah break down when we see the signs of Allah. Of course these verses in Surah Rum are much more but I have just sorted a few verses. “Wa min Aayaatihee yureekumul barqa khawfanw wa tama'anw wa yunazzilu minas samaaa'i maaa'an fa yuhyee bihil arda ba'da mawtihaaa inna fee zaalika la Aayaatil liqawminy ya'qiloon” 30:24 And among His Signs, He shows you the lightning, by way both of fear and of hope, and He sends down rain from the sky and with it gives life to the earth after it is dead: verily in that are Signs for those who are wise.

¶10 Actually Quran is insulting us. It says you do not understand, you do not hear, you do not reflect and you are not learned. When I look into these verses I think it’s insulting us. I don’t know about you. I feel that Quran is insulting saying that you do not understand, you are not learned and you do not reflect and do not hear. And of course the Quran tells us that some people have ears and eyes by which they do not hear and see. It is almost the same thing. But what is wrong with this? I mean this instrument of hearing does what work? It catches the sound. 10.15

¶11 However there is something inside which doesn’t catch it. There is a machine inside which is rust and doesn’t see these signs. We have heard these verses several times and sometimes some of us have felt that there are signs in this which we do not see. And just out of obedience ok you say there are signs so there are signs. It is fine but what we have to do to catch that sign, to hear, to reflect? Mysticism is all about making ones soul to hear, to see and to reflect. I think this is the summary of mysticism. If you want to make themselves hearing, seeing and reflect. This is the summary of Islamic Mysticism. All these things that inshaAllah we are going to discuss in the following lectures would tell us first of all how you can do that as it’s very difficult.

¶12 How can you prepare yourself to hear? There are lots of signs which you do not see. “Wa ka ayyim min Aayatin fis samaawaati wal ardi yamurroona 'alaihaa wa hum 'anhaa mu'ridoon” 12:105 And how many Signs in the heavens and the earth do they pass by? Yet they turn (their faces) away from them. We don’t see. Something is wrong. Now we put to in a very single expression, what is the sign to fix ones inner machine which is the soul? This is broken. It doesn’t work. Now we have to fix it to enable to catch the signals of god. And this is not of course a joke and not an easy path. It needs lots of training.

¶13 Self-trainings are done for many different purposes. Many mystics do self-training to find some powers for example or to be able to see the future or the past something like that. But Islamic mysticism is not about this course. Islamic mysticism is about catching the signs of Allah, to become sensitive to those signs and to hear and see. In some verses of the Quran which are very moving, “Qul ara'aitum in ja'alal laahu 'alaikumul laila sarmadan ilaa Yawmil Qiyaamati man ilaahun ghairul laahi yaa teekum bidiyaaa'in afalaa tasma'oon” 28:71 Say: See you. If Allah were to make the night perpetual over you to the Day of Judgment, what god is there other than Allah, who can give you enlightenment?

¶14 Are you not hearing? This is of course something catches the signals of god and beyond. What is beyond? The signs and the signals that god is sending to us and we have to catch it. There is a world I mean when you get prepared to get those signals then you have just started your machine and that machine can now work. And when it works then god knows what type of signals you can see and hear. It is not possible for us to reckon what mystics can see and hear. After that machine is fixed, the soul which is uplifted, god really knows what they see. I mean the things that the kaafir see and the imam sees of course they are the peak very peak of this type of people.

¶15 Now I’m sure some of you remember when we talked about muqarrabun and I will talk about it later on as well. We said the muqarrabun are of 4 categories, nabiyeen, siddiqeen, shohada and saleheen. Im sure I have talked about the first 3 groups. Saleheen I have never explained because it was not possible. I say that saleheen are very good. These are at the bottom of the category of muqarrabun. Of course muqarrabun as I said the prophets, immah, siddiqeen are muqarrabun. But ordinary people also can enter into the realm of muqarrabun and that realm of course makes them completely different from other people. And the Quran distinguishes them from other mominoon. However these salehun and of course it is very difficult to get into that last category of muqarrabun.

¶16 And that is what Islamic Mysticism is about. Can we find any evidence from our rivayat regarding this type of understanding because usually what we understand is that it’s only shariah. You follow shariah and you are successful and go to jannah. Ok that’s fair enough. That is something for ordinary mominoon. For muqarrabun, of course the whole terms and conditions are different. They are after something else. They are completely different. They are given jannah in this world itself. I mean in the other world they are after something else. And they become members of awliyaAllah. They become the proof of Allah. They are very different and these are actually the true urafah or mystics because mystic is a very general term.

¶17 We use it for Christian mystics, Hindu mystics, Buddhist mystics but aarif is a very nice term which we use in Islam when someone becomes true aarif. Now let’s see what beyond. We have all recited Munajat-e-Shabaaniyah. In this munajat it is mentioned that all our immah used to recite and supplicate with this munajat and it is reported from Imam Ali (as) and Imam Ali Zainul Abedeen(as)and all our immah used to recite. Now let’s see what we want from god and we are told to recite it. Sometimes I question why we are told to recite such words. I mean it’s like if you tell a primary school boy to read books of university. Really I mean these words are very hard.

¶18 They are at a peak of understanding and eagerness of muqarrabun. Here we are told to do this. “Ilahi hab li kamala alinqita`i ilayka wa anir absara qulubina bidiya'i nazariha ilayka hatta takhriqa absaru alqulubi hujuba alnnuri fatasila ila ma`dini al`azamati wa tasira arwahuna mu`allaqatan bi`izzi qudsika”. What does this mean? My lord, grant me complete severance of my relation with everything else. Is it good to completely cut off from everything else? Well, in the heart yes. We have it in the Quran “Wazkuris ma rabbika wa tabattal ilaihi tabteelaa” 73:8 cut off from everything and devote you to Him whole-heartedly. Now this is of course beyond that sensitivity which I mentioned from those verses and total submission to you.

¶19 Enlighten the eyes of our heart. If our eyes work then why we don’t see the signs? Because there is another mechanism which have to comply with what it receives. It doesn’t comply because it’s blind. Now the dua says it enlightens the eyes of our heart with the light of looking at you “bidiya'i nazariha ilayka”. What the mystics mean looking at god? Is it something possible at all? Quran says that you can never see god. Here it says bidiya'i nazariha ilayka. Not only can we see you “hatta takhriqa absaru alqulubi hujuba alnnuri” to the extent that the eyes of our heart penetrates the veils of light. What does this mean? The mystics of course talk about these things and sometimes people who are not familiar with the wordings say that these are made by mistake.

¶20 They say there are veils of light and darkness and someone should make through, penetrate through these veils until they reach to the very origin of the azamah and kibriya of Allah. Ok it’s here. The dua says it penetrates through the light and reaches the source of grandeur “fatasila ila ma`dini al`azamati”. This is of course something which we cannot understand, the source and grandeur of Allah. When we talk about Allah, when we talk about something which is not understandable because we cannot know and thing about. They want to know and look at him. They actually want to be attracted towards him. Of course they have to cut off from everything first. Teach me that severance from everything else until the eyes of my heart are enlightened and then I can look and penetrate through the veils of light and look into the source of grandeur and let our souls get suspended by the glory of your sanctity.

¶21 This is the meaning of your glory and santity. “Wa tasira arwahuna mu`allaqatan bi`izzi qudsika”. Our souls get suspended by the glory of your sanctity. Certainly we know what they are talking about. And if we don’t know what they are talking about it doesn’t mean that it is senseless and meaningless. Now my lord, make me one of those whom you call and they respond. This is something like prophets do. You call and they respond. And when you look at them they are struck by your majesty. “Ilahi waj`alni mimman nadaytahu fa-ajabaka wa lahaztahu fasa`iqa lijalalika”. You look inside their souls and they are thunder struck by the majesty that they see. This is munajat-e-shabaniyah. We cannot say that this is not good.

¶22 This is what all our immah have recited and we are told to recite this in the month of Shaban and I recommend that you recite this in the month of Shaban as much as you can. Of course we don’t understand many of the meanings of it but we have been honoured. This is very interesting. We have been honoured that you are allowed to recite because this is not in our capacity. This is not of our level but we have been honoured. Allah says ok you come and recite this, may be if your sincere inshaAllah I will grant you. What immah wanted, Allah granted them. Now one other sentence, most of the other sentences of this munajat are like this.

¶23 “Ilahi aqimni fi ahli wilayatika”. This talks about 2 meanings. One was marifah, understanding, looking at god, knowing him. The other is love for him. Marifah and love are the true meaning for wilayatik by which they can fly and these two are very things that they are asking. Incessant love for Allah and marifah which will ever be increasing and of course this will happen after that the machine is fixed and starts to work and show signal of Allah. “Ilahi aqimni fi ahli wilayatika muqama man raja alzziyadata min mahabbatika” Oh lord, place me among your friends in the position of one who hopes for an increase in your love. One who is finding the passionate love of remembering you so that he only remembers you.

¶24 “Ilahi wa alhimni walahan bidhikrika ila dhikrika wa himmati fi rawhi najahi asma'ika wa mahalli qudsika”. Now this is about I need to explain. If we look at other session of the dua as well, this is what I have actually taken for explaning the position muqarrabun. In Surah Waqiah we have this separation between mominun and muqarrabun. And muqarrabun are of course a group of people who are from awliyaAllah. Is that possible to get at that level of understanding, knowledge and love of Allah for a human being? Now we wrongly call ourselves human being. We are not yet human beings. We are animals who have potential to become human beings. Actually we are created as animals but we have that capacity to become a human being like the prophets who are real human beings.

¶25 A human being has the capacity to become a friend of god. Allah has created us at this strength and he wants us to reach that strength. Now well, for us we have become his enemy than becoming his strength. What makes these people different from others? Why in their ordinary life they can fix the machine? Then he says the description of awliyaAllah in Nahjul Balagah. I want to say awliyaAllah, we use it as synonym to the urafaa, the mystics. Imam Ali (as) says the lovers of Allah or the friends of Allah are those who look at the inward side of the world while the other people look at its outward. People look at what is on the surface.

¶26 The awliyaAllah looks deeper. That’s why they please Allah. They look deeper. But how they are able to do this? Why are we not able to do this? Because they busy themselves with 29:49 while the other people busy themselves in the imaging. For example it is wrong according to shariah to become rich. It is nothing wrong if you are rich. It’s just you get busy with these things. You can never reach that stage of awliyaAllah. They never think about themselves. They always think about god. They completely cut off from other things. Ordinarily we have family, we have friends, we have social position, we don’t think but in the heart we are completely cut off from him.

¶27 You are completely away and aloof from what goes on with other people. This is the short statement of sermon 432. I advise that you leave the rest to yourself because it is a very nice prescription of awliyaAllah. Let’s see Munajat-Khamsa Ashar which is in Sahifa-e-Sajjadiyah. If you look at this, it is from Imam Zainul Abedeen (as). You think that this is from someone who has actually left the society and lived in a cave and spent all his life dedicated completely to Allah. Now look what he says, “Ilaahee man daal-ladee daaqa halaawata mahab-batika faraama minka badalaa” who can have tasted the sweetness of you love and is after anything else. If you are after other things you have not tasted the sweetness of his love.

¶28 “Wa man daal-lade anisa biqur-bika fab taghaa anka hiwalaa” who is the one who used to be near him when they want to go somewhere else. They should map actually having the familiarity of the nearness of Allah as they want to go somewhere else. “Ilaahee faj-alnaa mim-man is-tafay tahoo liqur-bika wa wilaayatik” place us with whom you have chosen for your nearness, love and friendship. “Wa akh-lastahoo liwud-dika wa mahab-batik” and purify them completely for your love and affection. “Was haw-waq tahoo ilaa liqaa-ik wa razzay tahoo biqazaa-ik” and make them very eager to meet him with you. “Wa manah-tahoo bin-nazari ilaa wajhik” and you have given them a gift of looking at your face and they are able to look at your face.

¶29 Inshallah when we go to the lesson we will know what these sentences mean. Now it seems very meaningless but when we go through the course of the lesson we will know what is looking at the face of Allah. “Wa aad-tahoo min hajrika wa qilaak” and you have given refugee from the pain of separation from you. For some people it’s painful. When we call Allah, he is completely absent. We call him, we want to cry into the sky because we are very far away from him. For some people when they call him they feel the presence and actually respond in a way which makes them break down and faint like the immah. Sometimes when they call Allah they faint because they sense his nearness and the response so heavily.

¶30 “Watahoo bimaarifatik wa ahhal tahoo lil ibaadatik was hayyam taqal bahoo lil iraadaatik” you have chosen them for your true knowledge and made them worthy for worship of you and whose heart you have captivated with the will. This hayyamaan is more than that. It is worthy of love which never ever is quenched. And we have this about many angels wal malaikatil mohayyemeen, there are some angels who are actually burnt in the love of Allah. They just look at him in a way that they cannot turn their faces and we have in other sentences where the angels who are standing in a row watching you in a way that there are dumb. When other angels ask them anything they cannot hear, they cannot see.

¶31 They are completely absorbed to you and then give me that hayyamaan and of course we have some mystics who have felt this type of feel of Allah. Some mystics actually after finding this hayyamaan they couldn’t speak until the end of their life. I don’t say it is good because if they have enough capacity they can come back like the prophet goes to meraj and comes back. It needs great capacity of course on the side of the prophet and you have made his heart burn with the love of seeking you. InshaAllah I will find the translation and put it here and you have a look at this. This is how mystics works, islamic mysticism that we are talking about.

¶32 It is actually seeking and nothing else. It is not about any type of power or empowering the soul in a way to do karamat and mojezat. These are shirk. This is what Islamic mystism wants. Marefah and the love of Allah. How they do it and what will they find, this is the subject of our discussion.

¶33 Wa sallahu ala mohammadin wa aale hittahereen.
